title: The Water Tower
_comment: Intervals are the workout and the single source of truth for timing. Beats are narration placed at second offsets from the start. Total: 960s / 16 min, of which about 4 minutes is actual jogging.

beats.text: Runner Two, this is Ruby at Riverbend. I've got you on the radio. Start with an easy walk and warm those legs up.
Here's the situation. Our water tower sprang a leak last night. It made a sound like a giant slurping a milkshake. We need pipes.
The old hardware store is just down the road. In, out, easy. Oh, and there are a few zombies wandering about. But honestly? They are not very good at it.
Warm up's nearly done, Runner Two. Get those legs ready to jog.

beats.name: Water pipes
beats.text: Great jogging! Walk it out now. And look down, by the mailbox. Somebody dropped two water pipes. Grab them!
Two pipes in the bag. Riverbend is going to have water again because of you.
Keep it going! You are faster than anything out here.

beats.name: Jar of bolts
beats.text: Hardware store's just ahead, and the door is wide open. Shelf on your left. A jar of bolts. Two handfuls, that's plenty.
Uuuurgh. Snaaaacks?
Ha! That's just Gus. He has been trying to open the same jar of pickles for a month. Keep walking, he will never catch you.
Jogging again. Nice and light.

beats.name: Headlamp
beats.text: Hold on. On the counter there. A headlamp! Clip it on. That one is yours now, Runner Two.
Okay. Slight problem. Gus has friends. And they have noticed you.
Get ready to run. On my mark.
Go! Sprint to the end of the street! They are slow and you are fast. Run!
Almost there! Five more seconds! Four! Three! Two! One!
You lost them! And Gus tripped over a garden gnome. He's fine. He is apologising to it.
Walk it off, Runner Two. Big deep breaths. That was brilliant running.

beats.name: Wrench
beats.text: Wait. There's a wrench sitting in that flowerbed. We are definitely going to need that.
Home stretch now. Jog it out.

beats.name: Water pipes
beats.text: Two more pipes leaning against the fence. Last ones, I promise.
You know what? The kids at Riverbend have been asking about you. They call you the fast one.
Last jog of the day. Make it a good one!
That's it. That was the last one. Walk it home, Runner Two.
I can see you from the tower. Opening the gates now.
You're home. Slow it right down and shake those legs out.
Seven supplies and a headlamp. That is a proper haul. Take it to the base and start fixing that tower.
Get some rest. Next time we are going up the hill to the old radio mast. Ruby out.
